## Richardson Iteration

- Consider Problem 3(a), showing that the Pseudoinverse is a fixed point of the Richardson Iteration algorithm:

$$
x^{(k+1)} = x^{(k)} - \mu A^{T}\left(Ax^{(k)} - b \right)
$$

- Next Step: Substitute $A^{+}b$ for $x^{(x)}$:

$$ x^{(k+1)} = A^{+}b - \mu A^{(T)}\left(AA^{+}b - b\right)$$


## Most Common Mistake

- Many of you then concluded:

$$ AA^{+}b - b = 0$$

- Several justification, but:

```{r}
#| echo: true

A = matrix(rnorm(40),nrow=10,ncol=4)
b = rnorm(10)

t(A  %*% solve(t(A) %*% A) %*% t(A) %*%  b)


```
